```{r}
#| label: "index_common"
#| include: FALSE
if(file.exists(here::here("data/env.RData"))) file.remove(here::here("data/env.RData")) # Delete old environment on run
source("_common.R")
cache_network_resources <- TRUE
# TRUE  = reuse locally cached STRING/OmniPath resource tables when available
# FALSE = fetch/rebuild network resources normally
phosphosite_level <- FALSE
# TRUE  = individual phosphosite nodes and site-specific kinase edges
# FALSE = collapse each protein to the site with maximum abs(logFC)
#         and use the legacy STRING + phuEGO protein network
filter_sign <- FALSE
# TRUE removes only direct kinase-to-phosphosite edges whose known, non-zero
# signed experimental effects are opposite.
```

# For kinase activity and phosphosite integration, it is recommended to only use phosphosite_level==TRUE, as protein-level summarization may result in kinase-substrate_protein edges having illegitimate weights if a kinase phosphorylates a different site than the max(abs(logFC)) site   

This is a MultomicMenu report.

# Added database caching which sped up consecutive runs by 40-50% (~19 minutes down to ~11 minutes)
# Added a phosphosite category
# Added a boolean line for "phosphosite_level", when this variable is FALSE, the package has it's original behavior of each datatype contributing to gene-level nodes (phosphosite data are summarized by taking the max(abs(logFC)) site for each protein). When phosphosite_level=TRUE, each phosphosite gets it's own node, and kinase-site edges are included from PhosphoSitePlus and NetworKIN. 
# Revised the package to remove edges where kinase node is oppositely regulated to the connected phosphosite if filter_sign==TRUE and phosphosite_level==TRUE
# Added result file outputs to enable further analysis such as horizontal integration
